parsed.rationale: QS complexes in V1–V3 and deep T-wave inversions across V2–V5 show an anterior infarct, but the ST elevation in V2–V3 is only about 1.5–2 mm with inverted T waves, which looks like an evolved or old infarct (possibly an aneurysm pattern) rather than acute STEMI. This is borderline, so compare with a prior ECG and the clinical picture.
